title: An integral basis gives a rational continuous matrix
statement: Let K be a topological field, A a subring, L a sheaf of K_X-modules, e:L|U ≅ K_U^n, and P an integral lattice pair on V → U [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-pair-image-classification]. Fix finite local generators q of P.module which are bases. For a basis member q.X(i) and any arrow W → V factoring through it, there is G ∈ GL_n(C(|W|,K)) whose restriction to every T → W gives exactly e(P.image(T)) as its integral column span [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-section-matrix].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; An integral basis gives a rational continuous matrix

proof.text: Restrict the given integral basis to W and construct its section basis. The tensor sheafification unit at W is an isomorphism by the finite free neighborhood lemma. Compose its linear equivalence with the rationalization, the frame e, and free section coordinates to obtain a basis C of the rational coordinate module.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; An integral basis gives a rational continuous matrix

proof.text: If W is nonempty, evaluation at any point proves that its continuous K-valued section ring is nontrivial. Apply Module.Basis.indexEquiv over this commutative ring to reindex C by Fin n. The inverse coordinate equivalence of this basis supplies an invertible matrix G. Naturality of the integral basis, rationalization unit, and rational frame identifies every restricted column with the rational image of the corresponding integral basis section. Expand each integral section in that finite basis and distribute the finite sums to obtain both inclusions in the asserted integral matrix span. If W is empty, every T over W is empty, all target coefficients and free sections are subsingletons, and both images are the unique nonempty subset. Empty bases and n=0 are covered by the same finite sums.
